newsitem.title: TURKEY: Six Turkish MPs to face removal of immunity.
newsitem.headline: Six Turkish MPs to face removal of immunity.

text.p: Turkey's new government submitted proposals on Monday for the parliamentary immunity from prosecution of six MPs to be lifted, the state-run Anatolian news agency said.
The agency said dossiers prepared by the justice ministry were presented to the speaker of the parliament ahead of a possible vote in the assembly on lifting the MP's immunities.
Two of the deputies are independent Islamists, two are leftists and two are from the centre-right party of former prime minister Tansu Ciller.
One of the two outspoken Islamists is charged with "insulting and mocking" Turkey's secular armed forces.
The other, Sevki Yilmaz, is accused of the same with regard to the Turkish parliament.
His fiery rhetoric lay behind a fight which broke out at the weekend vote of confidence in NATO-member Turkey's new secularist government.
Leftist deputy Sabri Ergul enraged Islamist deputies by displaying a sign ordering Yilmaz -- who once called fellow deputies "pimps" -- to leave the chamber.
"Out with the biggest pimp," the sign read.
Furious Islamist deputies chased Ergul out of the parliament building amid chaos that forced speaker Mustafa Kalemli to suspend voting for 15 minutes.
The new anti-Islamist government led by Prime Minister Mesut Yilmaz won the vote.
Three others, including one-time deputy prime minister, Murat Karayalcin, are charged with abuse of office.

Deniz Baykal, whose left-wing party is supporting the government from outside the coalition, said after a meeting with Prime Minister Mesut Yilmaz that voting on the deputies should be held within one or two weeks.
